top_story.headline: Tiny super PAC admits late 48-hour reports and $23,870 donor refund tangle
top_story.dek: Vote Courage 4 Democracy Fund, formed in August, explained itself in a Form 99 filed October 5.
paragraphs: Vote Courage 4 Democracy Fund, an independent-expenditure-only committee formed in August 2026, filed a Form 99 on October 5 after notices from the FEC's Reports Analysis Division. Secretary and assistant treasurer James A. Barnett Jr. says the committee filed a paper Form 3X on August 14 without realizing that filing its Form 1 electronically had opted it into electronic filing, and that it will refile the 3X electronically with new transactions.
He also says the committee mistook its paper 3X for a 48-hour independent-expenditure report and is now filing the 48-hour report late for expenditures of $13,470 and $10,000.

The letter further says Barnett asked George Jordan to give personally so the fund could refund $23,870 in earlier donations from Jordan's business, Ansercall LLC. The fund's bank attributed the gifts to Jordan personally, which Barnett says was correct under the single-member-LLC rules, but they had already been refunded. The committee asks for leniency on late reports and says it expects no further spending above $10,000 this cycle.

sections.headline: Three sitting House members answered or received FEC letters
paragraphs: Two Republicans and one Democrat who currently hold House seats appear this edition. Kiggans for Congress and Adam Gray for Congress each answered an RFAI by Form 99, while Scott Fitzgerald for Congress received a new RFAI on cumulative totals in an amended 2025 report.

items: Rep. Jennifer Kiggans (R-VA-2), committee Kiggans for Congress — Form 99 answering a September 3 RFAI on the July Quarterly Report. Seven donors were flagged for apparent excessive contributions: Frank Ambrose, Geoffrey Pohanka and Thomas E. Robinson were refunded (July 21, July 17 and August 3); J. Murry Bowden was refunded September 1 after the committee found him duplicated in its donor database; Michael Ihrig was partly reattributed to his spouse Mary Ihrig; and Robert Loughney and William M. Somerindyke, Jr. were redesignated to the general election. The committee says all of it, plus attribution of an LLC gift from TMBSKYLO LLC to its partners, will appear on the October Quarterly Report, and it gave a general best-efforts answer on gifts from the Isle of Wight County Republican Party and John Reid for Virginia. Filing.

Rep. Adam Gray (D-CA-13), committee Adam Gray for Congress — Form 99 answering an August 30 RFAI: the July Quarterly Report's cumulative Column B totals were wrong on 16 lines (including 6(a), 11(b), 12, 15, 17, 21 and 22), and the committee says it has amended the report. The letter is signed by treasurer Lauren Decot Lee, who also signed for Villegas for Congress (see Form 99 section). Filing.

Rep. Scott Fitzgerald (R-WI-5), committee Scott Fitzgerald for Congress — RFAI dated October 4 on an amended July Quarterly Report for 2025 (04/01/2025–06/30/2025): the cumulative Column B totals on lines 6(a), 6(c), 11(c), 11(e) and 16 do not equal the prior report plus this period, and the FEC asked for an amendment covering all later reports as well. Response due 11/09/2026. Filing.

sections.headline: 46 RFAI letters, 27 of them missed-filing notices
paragraphs: The FEC's Reports Analysis Division sent 46 new RFAI letters dated October 4–5, led by 27 notices that committees may have skipped their September Monthly (and in two cases quarterly) reports. The rest ask for corrected cumulative totals, payroll and allocation detail, or fixes to registration forms; the three RFAIs for sitting members are in the Sitting Lawmakers section. Committee names are as FEC lists them; Shawn Hyms is treasurer of both America First Majority PAC and USA Patriots PAC, and Carolyn Denise Butler of Committee to Elect Sean Brown, which received two separate missed-filing notices (April and July Quarterly).

sections.headline: Committees answer RFAIs, explain refunds and report loan forgiveness
paragraphs: Most new Form 99 letters are replies to RFAIs sent in late August and early September, plus two paper loan-forgiveness letters. The most notable is the Vote Courage 4 Democracy Fund letter detailed in the Top Story; Mark Smith's forgiveness of $378,259.26 in loans is the largest dollar figure. Letters from Natalie Richoz's, Greenfield's and Frese's committees are one-off statements rather than RFAI replies.

items: Vote Courage 4 Democracy Fund — see Top Story. Signed by secretary and assistant treasurer James A. Barnett Jr.; admits a late 48-hour independent-expenditure report ($13,470 and $10,000), a paper-vs-electronic filing mix-up, and $23,870 refunded to donor George Jordan's business Ansercall LLC. Filing.

Jami Floyd for Congress — answers an August 31 RFAI on the April Quarterly Report: it amended the report to replace "Political Consulting" disbursement purposes with clearer ones and to add memo entries for a reimbursement to Sandor Weiss. Treasurer Cassie Tinsmon. Filing.

Villegas for Congress — answers an August 30 RFAI on the July Quarterly Report: a gift from Immigrants' List was dated 5/26 instead of 5/23 and will be corrected, and a contribution reported from Haystaq DNA was reattributed to Ken Strasma after the committee found it is a single-member LLC or sole proprietorship. Treasurer Lauren Decot Lee, who also signed for Adam Gray for Congress. Filing.

Lorenzo Rios for Congress — answers an August 30 RFAI about general-election contributions that had not been remedied: says all were timely refunded and will show on the October Quarterly Report. Treasurer Bradley T. Crate. Filing.

Build the Barn PAC — answers an August 31 RFAI listing donors who gave for the general election to Wahls for Iowa though Zach Wahls did not reach the general; says every donor was refunded within 60 days and more refunds will appear on the October Quarterly Report. Filed October 4. Filing.

Lone Star Liberty PAC — answers an RFAI: for a runoff election it filed a 24-hour independent-expenditure report as if it were a 48-hour report and so was one day late; it says staff have been trained on the rules. Filing.

Dem Turnout Fund (registered as Dem Turnout 2024) — answers a September 1 RFAI on collecting donors' employer and occupation: describes its best-efforts language on donation pages and a 30-day follow-up note to donors who leave the fields blank. Filing.

Montana Republican State Central Committee — answers a July Monthly Report RFAI: says utilities are included in its office rental agreement and that a payment to Ultra Graphics was correctly an administrative expense but mislabeled as donation envelopes; it will amend the description to letterhead and letterhead envelopes. Treasurer Bill Lussenheide. Filing.

Massachusetts Democratic State Committee – Fed Fund — answers a September 1 letter on the July Monthly Report: a contribution from the International Union of Painters and Allied Trades Political Action Together did not come from its federal account, so it was refunded and will be reported October 20; a gift from IBEW Local 103 Federal Political Action Committee did come from its federal account; and other federal operating expenses will go on line 21(b) going forward. Filing.

California Republican Party Federal Acct. (treasurer-signed by Bryan Burch) — four replies to FEC analyst Nicholas Tarone, all dated October 4: July Monthly (06/01–06/30/2026): says "Digital Media Consulting – less than 25% FEA" payments were administrative website, social-media analytics and graphic-design work that did not identify a federal candidate; June Monthly (05/01–05/31/2026): same explanation; amended February Monthly: says it amended the H4 schedule to match its H1 ratio, no over-transfer from its non-federal account, same consulting explanation; amended March Monthly: says the calculation error was fixed on the February amendment and no further amendment is needed. The committee also says it reports staff who spend over 25% of their time on federal election activity on line 30b and others on Schedule H4.

Richoz for Congress — submitted a House Ethics Committee late-fee waiver form signed by Natalie Richoz (dated 09/10/2026) for financial-disclosure and periodic transaction report filings due 05/01/2026, saying it accepts no donations, that no money changes hands and that any expense is paid personally. The filing refers to a Form 99 filed April 21, 2026. Filing.

Coloradans for Kerry Donovan — answers a September 2 letter on its residual cash: says it will keep the money for a possible future federal run by Kerry Donovan (no office or cycle identified) and that none will be used for personal use. Filing.
Theresa Greenfield for Iowa — says it intends to use residual campaign funds under FEC rules and not for personal use (reference: April and July 2026 quarterly reports). Filing.

Frese for Congress — says it has not exceeded $5,000 in receipts or spending through September 30, 2026, so it does not have to file the October Quarterly; it describes itself as the committee of Jeffrey Frese, a candidate in California's 10th District. Filing.

Timmins for Congress — paper letter from Patrick J. Timmins dated September 26, 2026 stating it is a statement of loan forgiveness, referencing its Termination Report (07/01–07/30/2026); the letter gives no dollar amount. Filing.

Mark Smith for Congress — paper letter from Mark Smith (treasurer Steve Martin), dated September 2, 2026 but stamped as received October 5, saying he forgave all personal loans to the committee, totaling $378,259.26. Filing.
Deliver Energize Succeed PAC — Notice of Paper Filing; the PDF had no readable text, so nothing beyond the filing type is known. Filing.
Massachusetts Republican Party — Form 99 whose PDF contains only a cover page and no message text, so its subject is not known. Filing.

sections.headline: Five Reversals and Refunds in Campaign Finance Records
paragraphs: Five large negative transactions appeared in federal campaign records this week, representing $195,650 in reversed or voided contributions. Negative amounts in FEC data conventionally indicate voided or refunded transactions—usually routine but occasionally the paper trail for something being unwound after the fact.
